metadata.archetype_justification: The system reads from an indexed employee master file (persistent state) and writes payout records — it owns data and performs write operations. No API surface exists (batch-only), no message queues, no downstream service calls. Classified as stateful-crud (conservative default for a stateful system without an API surface).

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on IBM z/OS mainframe (COBOL batch). The only cloud presence is a thin EC2 m4.large file gateway. No managed container orchestration or serverless.
findings.gap: All compute is on legacy mainframe with no managed cloud services.
findings.recommendation: Migrate payroll processing to managed compute — AWS Batch or Step Functions for batch workloads, or ECS/Fargate for containerized services after rewriting from COBOL.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: Database is IBM DB2 for z/OS v10, self-managed on mainframe. Employee data stored in VSAM-style indexed files. No managed database services in use.
findings.gap: All data persistence is self-managed on mainframe — no managed database services, no automated failover, no managed backups.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL or RDS PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS and SCT for DB2-to-PostgreSQL migration.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: Payroll workflow (read → calculate → write → FTP) is entirely hardcoded as sequential JCL steps and COBOL logic. No workflow orchestration service in use.
findings.gap: Multi-step payroll workflow hardcoded in JCL with no orchestration service, no retry logic, no error handling beyond JCL COND codes.
findings.recommendation: Implement payroll workflow using Step Functions with discrete orchestrated steps, error handling, and retries.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. Integration is via batch FTP file transfer only. For stateful-crud archetype, managed messaging is expected for cross-service state changes.
findings.gap: No messaging infrastructure — integration via unencrypted FTP. No event-driven notification when payroll completes.
findings.recommendation: Introduce EventBridge or SNS for payroll completion events. Use SQS for reliable delivery to downstream systems. Replace FTP with S3 + EventBridge notifications.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No VPC, subnet, security group, or network segmentation configuration exists. FTP connection transmits PII (SSN, bank accounts) unencrypted over the network.
findings.gap: No network security configuration — sensitive PII transmitted via plaintext FTP with no encryption in transit.
findings.recommendation: Define all networking in IaC with private subnets and restrictive security groups. Replace FTP with AWS Transfer Family (SFTP) or S3 with VPC endpoints.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or managed entry point exists. System communicates only via FTP. EC2 gateway accepts plain FTP connections directly.
findings.gap: No managed entry point — direct FTP access to EC2 gateway with hardcoded credentials.
findings.recommendation: Expose modernized payroll services behind API Gateway with authentication and throttling. Use AWS Transfer Family for file ingestion.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration exists. Fixed mainframe capacity and single static EC2 instance. No ASG, no ECS scaling, no Lambda concurrency.
findings.gap: All capacity statically provisioned — no ability to scale with demand.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling for compute (ECS/AWS Batch) and data (Aurora auto-scaling, DynamoDB on-demand) when migrating.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration exists in this repository. GDG datasets provide generational output only. No PITR, no cross-region replication, no documented restore procedures.
findings.gap: No backup configuration visible — no automated backups with defined retention.
findings.recommendation: Define backup strategy in IaC: automated daily backups with 30-day retention, PITR enabled, cross-region replication for DR.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Zero IaC exists. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any IaC files found. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage — all infrastructure manually created. No reproducibility, no DR automation.
findings.recommendation: Define all new cloud infrastructure in CDK or Terraform from day one. Codify VPC, compute, databases, file transfer, monitoring, and backup plans.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, CodeBuild, or any automation. All deployments manual.
findings.gap: Zero CI/CD automation — no build, test, or deploy pipelines.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD with CodePipeline + CodeBuild: automated build, unit test, integration test, and deployment stages with automated rollback.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Primary language is COBOL (Enterprise COBOL 4.2) with JCL for job control. COBOL has no AWS SDK and no cloud-native tooling ecosystem.
findings.gap: COBOL has no AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling. Skills are scarce (original author retired 2014).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language: Java 17+ with Spring Boot 3.x, Python 3.10+, or TypeScript/Node.js 18+.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith — single COBOL program handles all payroll logic with no module boundaries, no service interfaces, no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Single program with no clear module boundaries, pervasive shared state, all business logic in one procedure division.
findings.recommendation: Decompose into separate services: Employee Data, Tax Calculation, Pay Computation, Payment Disbursement. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All processing is synchronous batch. FTP transfer is synchronous. For stateful-crud archetype, cross-service communication should leverage async patterns but none exist.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. No message queues, no event-driven integration.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async communication for cross-service state propagation: SNS/EventBridge for payroll-complete events, SQS for reliable delivery.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Payroll batch runs 5-7 hours synchronously with no checkpointing, no status polling, no callbacks, no resume capability on failure.
findings.gap: 5-7 hour batch job with no async handling, no checkpointing, no status tracking, no resume-on-failure.
findings.recommendation: Implement with Step Functions: break batch into chunks with checkpointing and status tracking. Use DynamoDB for processing state.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No API versioning exists because no API exists. File format (fixed-width 120-byte records) is unversioned with no schema documentation.
findings.gap: No versioning of any interface — fixed-width file format is unversioned. Any format change breaks all consumers.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning from day one when building modernized payroll API. Add version header to file formats during migration.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: EC2 gateway IP (10.0.7.40) hardcoded in JCL source. No service discovery, no DNS resolution, no configuration externalization.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hardcoded in source code. Any infrastructure change requires source modification.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Cloud Map or DNS-based service discovery. Externalize endpoints into SSM Parameter Store.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Payroll output stored as fixed-width flat files on mainframe GDG datasets. Transferred via unencrypted FTP to EC2 gateway filesystem. Not in managed object storage.
findings.gap: Data on mainframe datasets and EC2 local filesystem — not in S3. No parsing pipeline, no accessibility for downstream systems.
findings.recommendation: Store all payroll output in S3 with structured formats (Parquet/JSON). Implement parsing pipeline. Enable S3 lifecycle policies.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Single COBOL program directly accesses employee master file via indexed file I/O. No data access layer, no repository pattern, no abstraction.
findings.gap: No data access abstraction — file access embedded directly in business logic.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern when rewriting to separate data access from business logic.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: IBM DB2 for z/OS v10 end-of-support since April 2020. Running unsupported 6+ years with no patches or vendor support.
findings.gap: Database engine 6+ years past EOL. No security patches, no vendor support, no compliance certifications.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL (latest) or RDS PostgreSQL 16. Use AWS SCT for schema conversion and DMS for data migration.

findings.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
findings.description: Business logic tightly coupled to IBM-proprietary data formats (VSAM indexed files, fixed-width EBCDIC records, GDG datasets). Functionally equivalent to proprietary data constructs.
findings.gap: Tight coupling to IBM-proprietary data formats requiring complete reimplementation for migration.
findings.recommendation: Extract all data access logic during rewrite. Define data model in database-agnostic SQL DDL. Convert VSAM to standard SQL queries.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured anywhere. Employee data including SSN and bank accounts stored in unencrypted VSAM files and GDG datasets.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for any data store — highly sensitive PII stored unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt all data at rest using KMS customer-managed keys for S3, RDS/Aurora, and EBS volumes.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No API authentication — only hardcoded static FTP credentials (username/password in plaintext JCL). Weaker than API key authentication.
findings.gap: No authentication mechanism beyond hardcoded FTP credentials visible in source control.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT via API Gateway authorizers backed by Cognito. Use AWS Transfer Family with IAM for file transfer. Rotate exposed credentials immediately.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. Hardcoded local username/password for FTP access. No Cognito, OIDC/SAML, SSO, or federation.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication entirely with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Cognito or organizational IdP). Implement SSO for admin access and IAM roles for service-to-service auth.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext credentials hardcoded in JCL source committed to git: username 'payroll' and password 'PayR0ll2003!'. No Secrets Manager, no Vault.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in version-controlled source code — critical security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate exposed credentials. Move all secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Eliminate FTP in favor of IAM-authenticated services.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching strategy, no vulnerability scanning, no compute hardening. Running end-of-support DB2 v10 confirms patching is not maintained.
findings.gap: No patching automation, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images. End-of-support software in use.
findings.recommendation: Use SSM Patch Manager, AWS Inspector, and hardened base images (Bottlerocket, Amazon Linux 2023) for new infrastructure.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists.
findings.gap: Zero security scanning — hardcoded credential would be caught by any basic secrets scanner.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST, dependency scanning, secrets detection, and container scanning into CI/CD from day one.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No tracing instrumentation — failures have no trace correlation.
findings.recommendation: Instrument modernized service with OpenTelemetry or X-Ray from day one.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms. Only implicit batch window mentioned in README (5-7 hours) but not formally defined or monitored.
findings.gap: No formal SLO definitions — no acceptable service levels defined or monitored.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for modernized service: batch completion within defined window, zero data loss, 100% employee coverage per run.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom business metrics published. No CloudWatch custom metrics for payroll outcomes. Only mainframe SYSOUT exists.
findings.gap: No business metrics — cannot track payroll outcomes or error rates programmatically.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics: employees_processed, total_gross_pay, processing_errors, batch_duration.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. Batch failures detected only when downstream systems notice missing files or employees report missing pay.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures detected reactively rather than proactively.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms for batch completion, error rates, and volume anomalies. Integrate with PagerDuty/OpsGenie.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. Changes validated only in manual shared QA region. Tax tables updated manually with no regression testing.
findings.gap: Zero automated testing — no regression safety net for a system processing employee pay.
findings.recommendation: Build comprehensive test suite: unit tests for tax calculations, integration tests for end-to-end payroll runs, regression tests using historical data.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No incident response automation. No runbooks, no SSM Automation, no self-healing. JCL references 'OPS RUNBOOK' but it does not exist in repo.
findings.gap: No runbooks, no automated incident response. Handling entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create operational runbooks for common failures. Implement automated remediation using SSM Automation or Step Functions.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarm ownership. System appears orphaned (original author retired 2014).
findings.gap: No observability ownership — system orphaned with no clear operational responsibility.
findings.recommendation: Establish clear ownership: CODEOWNERS, service-level dashboards, named alarm owners, documented escalation paths.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance
findings.description: No resource tagging. No IaC with tags, no tagging standards, no cost allocation tags.
findings.gap: No tagging governance — cannot track costs, ownership, or environment.
findings.recommendation: Define tagging standard and enforce via IaC: required tags for service, team, environment, cost-center.
